options.A: The unconditional subordination of the economy to any political will
options.B: The identity of economic and political relations
options.C: The independence of political decisions from production
options.D: Mutual influence, with material constraints on politics
options.E: The one-sided determination of politics by current prices

options.A: The state's lack of distributive functions
options.B: The impossibility of political influence on distribution
options.C: The inevitability of direct democracy during an economic downturn
options.D: The dependence of decisions on the material conditions of their implementation
options.E: The fundamental independence of law from the economy

options.B: The impossibility of discussing the consequences of decisions
options.C: The complete coincidence of law with moral judgment
options.E: The incompatibility of morality with group interests in general

options.B: The psychological motives of every voter
options.C: The economic efficiency of every decision
options.D: The basic principles of its organization in legislation

options.D: The independence of power from normative restrictions
options.E: The elimination of political conflict by a legal act

options.B: Explaining behavior by innate biological properties
options.C: Explaining decisions by the distribution of competence among bodies

options.E: Deriving order from the prevailing class relations

options.D: Sociocultural characteristics influence the choice of political values
